thingsToDo.title: Explore Flatirons
thingsToDo.description: The Flatirons are a series of steeply tilted sandstone formations on the eastern flank of Green Mountain above Boulder, visible from much of the city and the University of Colorado campus. The slabs were formed through uplift and erosion processes associated with the Laramide Orogeny, then exposed as dramatic west-dipping outcrops. Much of the surrounding foothill landscape is protected within Boulder’s open space and Chautauqua area, where trail systems provide access to multiple viewpoints. Their geologic age, orientation, and proximity to the urban grid make the Flatirons both a scientific landmark and a civic symbol. They are central to Boulder’s identity as a Front Range city where mountain terrain begins immediately at the city edge.
